name: Binary Volume Ray Casting with Lookup Table
definition: A rendering technique that uses a binary volume B to skip empty regions. It finds the first non-zero byte via binary search and uses a 256-entry lookup table (LUT) to determine the bit position within that byte, avoiding the allocation of a $2^{32}$ byte array.
summary: Binary Volume Ray Casting with Lookup Table accelerates finding the first volume intersection by using a binary mask to skip empty regions and a compact lookup table to locate the hit, avoiding the memory overhead of direct addressing.
